title: A Soldier's Course, from Battles Won
description: A Soldier's Course, from Battles Won in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Gisborne wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 340 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Christian's Life and his Hope”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A sol-dier's course, from bat-tles won To new com-menc-ing strife; A pil-grim's, rest-less as the sun Be-hold the Christ-ian's life!

lines: A soldier's course, from battles won
A pilgrim's, restless as the sun —
O! let us seek our heavenly home,
The land whence pilgrims never roam,
Where grief shall never wound, nor death,
The land where, suns and moons unknown,
Where they who meet shall never part;
Dwells face to face with man.

licence: Public domain: Thomas Gisborne died in 1846.
credits: Words by Thomas Gisborne (1758–1846), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
